neighbours.label: The element symbol of a bracketed noble-gas core in an electron configuration ('[He]', '[Ne]', '[Ar]' before 2s2, 3s1 ...); quiet on the same elements named in ordinary prose or configurations written without a bracketed core.
fire: Lithium, with three electrons, is written as [He] 2s1 in shorthand.
The shorthand for magnesium is [Ne] 3s2, with two valence electrons.
Potassium has the configuration [Ar] 4s1, which explains its reactivity.
For carbon, chemists write [He] 2s2 2p2 to show the outer shell.
The configuration of rubidium is [Kr] 5s1, much like potassium.
Chlorine is written [Ne] 3s2 3p5, one electron short of argon.
Calcium has the configuration [Ar] 4s2 and forms Ca2+ ions.
In the table, nitrogen appears as [He] 2s2 2p3 with three unpaired electrons.
quiet: Lithium, with three electrons, is used widely in rechargeable batteries.
Magnesium burns with a bright white flame when it is heated.
Potassium is found in bananas and helps regulate blood pressure.
For carbon, chemists write 1s2 2s2 2p2 to show every shell.
Rubidium was discovered in 1861 by Bunsen and Kirchhoff.
Chlorine gas was used to clean the water in the city pool.
Calcium is important for strong bones and healthy teeth.
In the garden shed, the old neon sign still hangs above the door.

predictions: median fire ~0.45 (probes: '[He] 2s2' 1.05, '[Ne] 3s1' 0.52); near misses < 0.15 (helium balloons 0.04, iron and calcium 0.08). Risk: weaker material pieces like 'monoclinic' 0.45 are not tested.
notes: Card mixes element symbols in formulas, configurations and crystallography pieces; SiO2-style formulas scored low in probes (0.045), so the test targets configuration cores only. '[Xe]' splits into X+e, so it is avoided.
